readerMoment: Has typed one-line prompts into an AI video generator and gotten clips back that drift, wander, or try to do three things at once. Has a story idea and has never planned a shot.
outcome: Can produce one coherent 8-10 second clip from their own story idea by giving it one beat, a deliberate start frame, and a static or motivated camera, and can say why the result holds together.
coreModel: A clip holds together when it carries exactly one beat, and everything the model needs is either a parameter or a picture, not a wish in prose.

teachingShape.realTask: Take your own story idea and produce one 8-10 second clip that a stranger could describe in one sentence.
activate: Your last mushy clip: name the two or three things it tried to do; that crowding is the failure this page removes
Your one-line prompt habit: everything was a wish, nothing was decided
demonstrate: One worked shot from a small story idea: 'a woman crosses a kitchen at dawn and opens the window' - planned as container settings first (duration, aspect, resolution in the tool), one beat, a chosen start frame, framing named (medium), camera static, and the action written as timed beats that fit the seconds
The same idea prompted the one-line way, shown failing: the model improvises the kitchen, the camera wanders, the beat blurs
apply: Write your shot plan on the same skeleton: container settings, the one-beat sentence, the start frame description, framing, camera decision, timed action beats
Choose or make your start frame and generate two or three takes in your generator
Check what your generator actually supports today (first frame? fixed seed? references?) against its own docs, not memory
integrate: Pick the take that holds and say why in one line: one beat, anchored first frame, camera with a reason
Record the plan, the settings, and the winning take in your own shot log - the page's fields reset when you leave, so the record lives in your notes

requiredIdeas: Container versus prose: duration, resolution, and aspect are parameters set in the tool; the prompt cannot make a clip longer, only better directed.
One beat per clip: the 8-10 second length is a discipline, not a limit; two beats in one clip is the mush failure.
The first frame anchors the whole generation: in image-to-video the input image acts as the first frame, so choosing it is directing.
Framing is a choice with a meaning: wide establishes, medium carries interaction, close carries feeling.
The camera is static or motivated: every move must tell the viewer something, or it reads as generated.
Action is written as timed beats ('crosses four steps, pauses, opens the window in the final second'), not adverbs; the beats must fit the duration.
Takes are cheap: generate two or three and pick, because the same prompt gives different results by design.
Capability claims expire: what your generator supports (first frame, keyframes, references, seeds) is checked against its current docs, dated.
candidateAnalogies: Prompting is briefing a cinematographer who has never seen your storyboard: leave it out and they improvise.
A shot is one sentence of the story, not a paragraph.
The start frame is the opening note the whole clip harmonizes with.
visualNeeds: The same beat framed three ways (wide, medium, close) side by side, so the framing choice is seen, not described
A worked shot plan skeleton filled in for the kitchen example: container, beat, start frame, framing, camera, timed beats
A spatial seam picture for the failed one-line generation: wandering camera path versus the planned static frame

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Chaining clips together (end frame to start frame)
deliberatelyExcluded.why: Page 3's job. One honest shot comes before any seam; chaining a mushy shot chains the mush.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Character references, cameos, and multi-image consistency
deliberatelyExcluded.why: Page 2's job. Consistency across generations is its own discipline and needs the one-shot craft first.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Step-by-step walkthroughs of one generator's interface
deliberatelyExcluded.why: Capabilities and layouts change monthly; the page teaches the decisions and points at the dated docs.
Native audio exists on some generators but the shot craft here is visual; sound is a later series.
Meaningless before clips chain; scoped to page 4.

nextPagePressure: Your one shot holds together. Now the same character, the same light, and the same room have to survive the next generation - and prose alone will not keep them.
